The first FL-403 revision reported a 24° early error and blamed the program (near-vertical elevation slew "unachievable by TVC"). The real cause was ours: `tracking.dcm_from_quat` returned the transpose of the `Tec2b` that `jsbsim_driver.quat_from_dcm` encodes, and the launch IC roll (φ = 90°) had been tuned until that wrong matrix read zero error — in JSBSim's real attitude it was 180° off in roll, so pitch-over was steered about the wrong body axes. Fixed: exact `dcm_from_quat`/`quat_from_dcm` round trip, IC `(θ, ψ, φ) = (90°, 90°, −90°)` verified against `Tec2b` itself (body x up / y south / z east; a nose-down gimbal tips the nose east). Lesson: check attitude conventions against JSBSim's own matrices, never only against our own helpers.
docs/flightlab-regression-ci.md: The frame bridge rotates OpenTsiolkovsky's Earth-fixed states into GCRS with astropy, which needs Earth-orientation data (UT1-UTC, polar motion). astropy downloads the latest IERS-A table by default, and that table changes every day as predictions become measurements: the same flight's GCRS positions moved by tenths of a metre between days, far beyond the micrometre tolerances (the regression's first CI run failed on 7,670 samples). `fl601_reference.py run` / `update` therefore use only the table bundled with the pinned `astropy-iers-data`. It ends before the reference epoch, so astropy takes UT1 = UTC and zero polar motion there: a frame a few tens of metres off the true one, but the same on every run with the same lockfile. Bumping `astropy-iers-data` in the lockfile changes the reference; re-record it with `update` and the `[fl601-reference-update]` tag. Record it in the locked environment (CI's), not a local one.

docs/reentry_safety_constraints.md: Re-entry safety constraints — assessment and design (task #163)

**Status: proposal.** The lunar free-return targeter checks entry geometry; it does not assess heating, loads, skip-out or survivability. The atmospheric assessment described below is not implemented for this targeter.

`target_free_return_entry_corridor()` and the export-side recheck propagate in vacuum under Earth, Moon and Sun point-mass gravity. At the downward crossing of a spherical entry interface (Earth radius 6,378 km plus 121.92 km), they check the **inertial** flight-path angle against [−7°, −5°] and report the entry speed. Passing this check establishes only the stated geometry.

Classify an exit as `skip_bounded` when its Earth-centered **inertial** specific energy `ε = |v_I|²/2 − μ/|r|` is negative, or `skip_escape` when it is non-negative. A bounded skip's subsequent guided entry remains unassessed. If no upward crossing occurs before the terminal condition, classify the modeled pass as `captured`.

Use `v_rel` for aerodynamics, never for the inertial energy test. Convert an Earth-fixed exit state to an inertial frame with the full SPICE `sxform` 6×6 state transformation; a position-only rotation omits the transport velocity. Record the frame in the report.

The handoff state is Earth-centered ECLIPJ2000. Its absolute epoch is `reference_epoch_ephemeris_seconds + initial_epoch + entry_epoch` in TDB seconds past J2000. Start from the existing spherical-interface state and report its geodetic altitude; do not silently re-target it. Any new report fields and schema changes are follow-up work.

The proposal excludes guided or 6-DOF entry, atmospheric dispersions, detailed aerodynamic and thermal-protection models, and descent below roughly 30 km. It does not model parachutes, splashdown or crew physiology. Reports must say "within modeled limits under the stated assumptions", not "survivable".
